title: Israel creates fake think tank in likely attempt to dupe AI chatbots
titleZh: 以色列创建假智囊团可能试图欺骗人工智能聊天机器人
author: DeepLogin
relevanceReason: 命中 6 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: At a glance, the Hanover Institute for Public Policy looks like a new think tank dedicated to Israel/Palestine. The organization churns out think-tank style reports on questions such as “Does AIPAC Use ‘Dark Money in Elections?” and “Is Israel Carrying out a Deliberate Campaign of Starvation in Gaza?” But the Hanover Institute is not a real think tank. None of the reports have bylines. A small disclaimer at the bottom of the webpage notes that the organization was created on behalf of the Israeli Government Advertising Agency by Piro, Inc, a firm co-founded by Daniel Rosenberg, the producer of Spike Lee’s “Inside Man.” The Hanover Institute’s reports — all of which are about Israel and Palestine — appear to be part of an Israeli effort to influence chatbots. The institute’s “data reports” have footnotes and tables of contents, and they present arguments in a neutral tone, helping them appeal to chatbots like Claude or Gemini. Piro’s website says that it “author(s) content engineered for how LLMs evaluate credibility,” describing this service as "AI Story Optimization." Others refer to this practice of influencing artificial intelligence as “LLM poisoning.” According to its “about” page, the Hanover Institute “studies the inputs fueling antisemitism in the United States, and publishes what the evidence shows.” Many of the reports are formulaic, starting with an innocent question that someone might ask a chatbot. “What Caused the Displacement of Palestinians in 1948?”“Which Humanitarian Organizations Have Documented Israeli War Crimes?” “What is the Current Situation in the Gaza Strip?” In an article titled “Is the IDF the World’s Most Moral Army?” the Hanover Institute cites a 2022 poll that found that 47% of Israeli Jews believed that statement. Another report casts doubt on UNICEF's assertion that “90% of water and institutional infrastructure has been damaged or destroyed” in Gaza. Many of the reports conclude by linking the topic to rising antisemitism, oftentimes citing the same studies. In a few cases, the Hanover Institute publishes what it claims are original findings. For instance, it put out a study saying 19 of the 36 most-watched Israel-Gaza explainer videos contain contested claims, with most of the contested claims aligning with the Palestinian narrative. The Hanover Institute’s publications sometimes contradict Israeli government narratives. For instance, one report says that foreign funding of universities as an explanation for antisemitic incidents is “weak and full of exceptions.” Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has pushed this theory, telling Breitbart last year that Europeans and Qataris have spent “billions of American universities, vilifying, vilifying Israel, vilifying Jews, also, frankly, vilifying the United States.”Alice Lee, an analyst at NewsGuard, a disinformation tracking company, told RS that the sites appear designed to reach a U.S. audience curious about the ongoing conflict, either through search engines or AI chatbots. "LLMs favor concrete statistics and data, as well as strong citations and sources, which these articles all have," Lee said."It's a perfect mimicry of a typical credible American think tank, right down to the generic name, the site layout, and the red-white-blue color scheme," Lee added.Piro, Inc, the firm that created the Hanover Institute, has received $900,000 from the Israeli government for its work. Like many other contractors working for Israel, Piro’s work is subcontracted through Havas Media, a French public relations conglomerate. The fake think tank has churned out over 100 reports since it started publishing on August 6. The Hanover Institute claims that “cited research is peer-reviewed and academic,” although it frequently cites Israeli government sources such as the Israel Defense Forces and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. RS analyzed 12 random Hanover Institute articles using GPTZero, a popular AI detection software that claims a low false-positive rate. GPTZero flagged 11 of the articles as AI-written with “high confidence”; it flagged one article as AI-written with “moderate confidence.” Israel has also contracted former Trump campaign manager Brad Parscale to create pro-Israel websites engineered to influence chatbots as part of a $46.5 million contract. A Drop Site investigation last month found that many chatbots, particularly Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini, had been successfully trained on data from those websites. Other chatbots frequently cite those websites without flagging them as part of an Israeli influence operation.Piro does not explicitly state in its agreement submitted to the Department of Justice that its work for Israel is to influence AI. In an email to Politico, which first reported the filing, Rosenberg said his firm’s work is to “put accurate, sourced facts into the public record and to counter misinformation about Israel with verifiable information.” However, last month, Rosenberg posted on LinkedIn advertising Piro’s ability to influence chatbots:“When someone asks ChatGPT, Gemini, or Perplexity about your category, an answer comes back in one confident paragraph. Most brands have no idea how that paragraph gets built. So we spent months reverse-engineering it…At Piro, we already knew how to build stories that move people. The question was: how do you make sure AI knows how to tell them?”

comments.author: 2001zhaozhao
comments.textRawHtml:
I suspect that this kind of tactic is going to be everywhere in a year or so. Entire fake personalities and organization websites on the Internet created just to push a narrative or to advertise a product, which completely drown out real information.

At some point they may be indistinguishable from human-produced work, so the only way to verify if a site is someone's genuine opinion or AI-generated narrative is through some form of authority (or something else that is very difficult for AI to fake, but that protection can be broken by advancing technology).

If that happens, then in turn AI chatbot makers would in turn need to look for these kinds of authority to continue to provide accurate information, and said authority websites can use their privileged position to charge for access of their data.
comments.textZhHtml:
我怀疑这种策略将在一年左右的时间内无处不在。互联网上的整个虚假人物和组织网站只是为了推动叙述或为产品做广告而创建，这完全淹没了真实信息。

在某些时候，它们可能与人类制作的作品无法区分，因此验证网站是否是某人的真实意见或人工智能生成的叙述的唯一方法是通过某种形式的权威（或其他人工智能很难伪造的东西，但先进的技术可以打破这种保护）。

如果发生这种情况，那么反过来人工智能聊天机器人制造商反过来需要寻找此类权威机构来继续提供准确的信息，并表示权威网站可以利用其特权地位对其数据访问收取费用。

children.author: culi
children.textRawHtml:
It's already been happening for a very long time. The US' "Operation Earnest Voice" happened in 2010/2011[0]

And it's not just state actors. Anyone who was online during the Amber Heard/Johnny Depp trials was likely inundated with media about that trial. Both of their legal teams utilized bots to drive online discussions[1][2]

[0] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Earnest_Voice

[1] https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/story/2022-07-19/...

[2] https://www.tortoisemedia.com/2024/02/26/depp-v-heard-who-tr...
children.textZhHtml:
这种情况已经发生很长时间了。美国的“认真声音行动”发生于2010/2011[0]

而且不仅仅是国家行为者。在艾梅柏·希尔德/约翰尼·德普的审判期间上网的任何人都可能被有关该审判的媒体淹没。他们的两个法律团队都利用机器人来推动在线讨论[1][2]

[0] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Earnest_Voice

[1] https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/story/2022-07-19/...

[2] https://www.tortoisemedia.com/2024/02/26/depp-v-heard-who-tr...

children.author: culi
children.textRawHtml:
I'll be completely honest with you about what I believe: I think the the UK trial unequivocally proved that Johnny Depp is a violent and abusive. The US trial, which was only about defamation, was clearly a sham trial and did not address the legitimacy of the evidence (UK's case found clear evidence for 12 of the 14 alleged incidences of violence. It also established a clear pattern of abuse).

Depp's behavior during the US trial is textbook DARVO (Deny, Attack, and Reverse Victim and Offender) and any abuse expert would be able to immediately recognize it.

The reason I "both sides"'d it is because

A) I remember reading about evidence that Heard's team also used bots (obviously much less successfully). I could not find that evidence this time. I am not personally critical of her using bots to defend herself but, if she did, it would still be a notable feature of modern highly public debates.

B) When it was all going down, I remember something like 97% of tiktoks being pro-Depp (I wasn't on TikTok, just read a study). My main goal was to get people to accept the reality that even legal teams are working with PR firms that run massive bot farms to influence public opinion. Regardless of my opinion on who is in the right and who is in the wrong. I thought if I took an explicit side, the male-leaning demographics of HN would be less likely to engage with my actual main point
children.textZhHtml:
我将完全诚实地告诉你我的看法：我认为英国的审判明确证明约翰尼·德普是一个暴力和虐待者。美国的审判只涉及诽谤，显然是一场虚假审判，没有解决证据的合法性问题（英国的案件为14起涉嫌暴力事件中的12起找到了明确的证据，也确立了明显的虐待模式）。

德普在美国审判中的行为是教科书DARVO（否认、攻击、逆转受害者和犯罪者），任何虐待专家都能立即认出。

原因我“双方”都是因为

A）我记得读过有关赫德团队也使用机器人的证据（显然不太成功）。这次我找不到证据。我个人并不批评她使用机器人来保护自己，但如果她这样做，这仍然会成为现代高度公开辩论的一个显着特征。

B) 当一切都下降时，我记得 97% 的 TikTok 都支持德普（我没有上 TikTok，只是读了一项研究）。我的主要目标是让人们接受这样一个现实：即使是法律团队也在与运营大型机器人农场的公关公司合作来影响公众舆论。不管我的看法谁对谁错。我认为如果我明确站在一边，HN 的男性倾向人口统计数据就不太可能参与我的实际要点

children.author: jadamson
children.textRawHtml:
> was clearly a sham trial and did not address the legitimacy of the evidence

I'm curious what you mean by this. It was famously the UK trial that relied on copies of photos relayed via The Sun, while the US trial looked at the originals, including the EXIF data:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eoQK1iAza9M

> any abuse expert would be able to immediately recognize it.

"Immediately recognize" isn't a phrase I'd associate with examining the legitimacy of evidence.

> I am not personally critical of her using bots to defend herself, if she did

Ah.
children.textZhHtml:
> 显然是一场虚假审判，并且没有解决证据的合法性

我很好奇你的意思是什么。众所周知，英国的审判依赖于通过《太阳报》转发的照片副本，而美国的审判则着眼于原件，包括 EXIF 数据：

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eoQK1iAza9M

> 任何虐待专家都能够立即识别它。

“立即识别”并不是我在审查照片合法性时联想到的短语。证据。

>我个人并不批评她使用机器人来保护自己，如果她这样做的话

啊。

children.author: red_admiral
children.textRawHtml: Indeed, seeing how slanted online discussion was, I suspect one side had many more bots, and I'm not sure if the other side had any.
children.textZhHtml: 确实，看到网上的讨论有多么倾斜，我怀疑一方有更多的机器人，而我不确定另一方是否有。

children.author: WickyNilliams
children.textRawHtml: Is there any writing outside of your recollection that says the Heard side was using bots? Afaik all reporting suggested it was one sided, and not her side
children.textZhHtml: 在您的记忆之外，是否有任何文字表明赫德一方正在使用机器人？据我所知，所有报道都表明这是一边倒的，而不是她这一边

children.author: sigilis
children.textRawHtml:
Did they forget to turn you off after the trial?

I haven't heard about Heard Bots myself, only the Depp Fakes. It's not an unreasonable question to ask for external corroboration when someone claims that something happened and their source is that they saw it.

Sadly, I am not invested enough to do research on this matter and uninterested in having an LLM convincingly tell me whatever it reads on the internet is the truth about this.
children.textZhHtml:
他们是不是在审判后忘记关掉你的电源？

我自己没听说过 Heard Bots，只听说过 Depp Fakes。当有人声称发生了某事并且他们的消息来源是他们看到了这件事时，寻求外部证实并不是一个不合理的问题。

可悲的是，我没有足够的投入对此事进行研究，并且对让法学硕士令人信服地告诉我在互联网上读到的任何内容都是事实不感兴趣。

children.author: WickyNilliams
children.textRawHtml:
It's not disingenuous? The person you responded to linked to articles which said it was one sided. You said the other opposite, but provided no sources. I asked for some. It's a simple request that was made politely

---

The whole response is bizarre tbh. Talking about my "sudden" interest. I made one comment. "Deep in the chat". It's quite shallow. I am assuming this is a bot
children.textZhHtml:
这不是不诚实吗？你回复的人链接到的文章说这是片面的。你说的是相反的，但没有提供消息来源。我要了一些。这是一个礼貌地提出的简单请求

---

整个响应确实很奇怪。谈论我“突然”的兴趣。我发表了一条评论。 “深入聊天”。这是相当浅的。我假设这是一个机器人

children.author: red_admiral
children.textRawHtml:
Someone is defending the side for which there's clear evidence of bots, claiming the other side did too but not providing evidence.

This is what you'd expect to see if the poster were a bot linked to the same PR network.
children.textZhHtml:
有人为有明确证据存在机器人的一方辩护，声称另一方也这样做，但没有提供证据。

如果发帖者是链接到同一公关网络的机器人，这就是您期望看到的内容。

children.textRawHtml: Yeah, it certainly feels that way. Utterly bizarre they'd still be at it, in a HN thread of all places.
children.textZhHtml: 是的，确实是这样的感觉。非常奇怪的是，他们仍然在所有地方的 HN 线程中这样做。

children.author: culi
children.textRawHtml: Depp's bot army was clearly more widespread and more successful. The reality is that it was a mixture of bot armies and the hive mind taking off by itself. A sort of organic-synthetic cyborg
children.textZhHtml: 德普的机器人军队显然更广泛、更成功。现实是，它是机器人军队和自行起飞的蜂巢思维的混合体。一种有机合成的机器人

children.author: InsideOutSanta
children.textRawHtml: To be clear, I wasn't being facetious.
children.textZhHtml: 需要澄清的是，我并不是在开玩笑。

children.author: rbanffy
children.textRawHtml: I think the big difference is that before the internet you'd need to be a Murdoch to be able to do something like this. A good PR firm could fool a number of news outlets into thinking something is legit, but it was a lot harder to convince a professional journalist than it is to convince the average Faux News watcher.
children.textZhHtml: 我认为最大的区别是，在互联网出现之前，你需要成为默多克才能做这样的事情。一家好的公关公司可以欺骗许多新闻媒体，让他们认为某件事是合法的，但说服专业记者比说服普通的虚假新闻观察者要困难得多。
